blocked: Own site (ordertacoselninosantana.com) embeds a MenuStar ordering widget (139 items across 21 categories, address 7287 El Cajon Blvd confirmed on page). Prices are heavily scattered-cent ($3.64, $4.11, $16.90, $19.76, etc.) with no round-dollar pattern in the raw payload. A divisor sweep found 84% (129/153) of prices resolve to round numbers when divided by 1.04, suggesting a baked-in ~4% fee - but a direct item-level cross-check against a Grubhub listing at the same address is inconsistent with a single uniform fee: 'Orden De Tamales' matches exactly ($5.00 = $5.00, no markup) while 'Carne Asadas Fries' does not (MenuStar $16.90 vs Grubhub $15.25, matching description 'Guacamole, crema y queso', a ~10.8% gap). Since neither the uniform-fee theory nor a trustworthy single source holds up under direct comparison, this is blocked rather than filed with either scattered or divided prices. Needs a browser to read Grubhub's or Yelp's full rendered menu (both are JS-rendered shells to a plain curl) for a clean cross-check, or a dine-in/photo menu.
